title: My AI bot made +$134k on a 100k FTMO 1-Step backtest. Should I loosen max DD to grow profit?
author: PrestigiousAdagio555
selftext:
Hey all, I'd like some honest feedback before going live.

**Setup**  
Multi-agent AI trading system, 5 instruments (gold included)  
Built specifically for the FTMO 1-Step 100k challenge  
Backtest from Jan 2025 to now: **+$134k** on a 100k account  
Daily DD capped at 2.5–2.7%, hard max DD cap at 9.5%  
Monte Carlo: passes the challenge **\~100% of runs**, daily DD always under the limit, worst max DD around 9.2%  
I haven't tested it live or forward yet. That's the next step.

**The dilemma**  
To push profit higher I'd have to raise the max DD, and then Monte Carlo starts showing failed challenges.

**Questions**  
For a prop challenge, is profit even the right thing to optimize? The target is +10%. Should I optimize for speed and survival instead?  
Would you run a different risk profile for the challenge and for the funded phase?  
My Monte Carlo reshuffles trades from the same backtest. How do you stress test beyond that?  
How long would you forward test on demo before buying the challenge?  
What red flags am I missing? A 100% pass rate feels too good to be true.  
Thanks, I can share more details in the comments.

comments.author: DatGiantIsopod
comments.body:
You haven't mentioned costs anywhere in your post, so first thing I'd ask is how you're modelling slippage in your backtest, and then stress testing would involve doubling or tripling it, and also ensure fees are correctly taken into account. Other things are blind holdouts, how does it perform on 2024-2025 and other periods? Then do placebo runs and neighbour settings etc. There's a lot more you can do than just Monte Carlo, but since you never mentioned costs I'd certainly start there.

If it passes all that, then yeah loosening DD is fine imo. But that's personal to you and what you can tolerate if it was real money. I've been in crypto for a long time holding through winters etc so most of the drawdowns associated with trading are like kitten kisses lol.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
The 100% pass rate is the part I'd worry about. Reshuffling trades from the same backtest only changes the order of the same trades, it can't show you what happens if the edge itself is weaker than it looks. I'd shave a bit off every trade or randomly drop some of the winners, and see where the pass rate starts to break.

And yeah, for the challenge I'd optimize for not failing. Hitting +10% is the whole job there, extra profit doesn't buy you anything.

comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body:
good points above on costs and shaving the edge. one more that matters a lot for a multi-agent AI system specifically: if the agents are LLMs, the backtest period (Jan 2025 to now) is very likely inside or close to their training data. the model may simply "know" how gold and the rest moved in that stretch, even if you never told it, and that leaks straight into the decisions. that alone can make a backtest look like +134k. for LLM-driven systems I only trust forward results on data after the model's training cutoff.

so on "how long to forward test": I'd run it on demo until you have at least a few dozen trades spread over 2-3 months, with the exact settings frozen, and compare it with the backtest month by month. if forward looks like a weaker version of the backtest, fine. if it's a different animal, the backtest was the leak.

also, worst max DD 9.2% against a 10% hard limit isn't much room. one slippage day or one bad fill on gold and the 100% becomes a fail. for the challenge I'd go the other way from your question: lower risk, take longer to hit +10%, since there's no prize for getting there fast.

comments.author: k1_r1
comments.body:
on the challenge vs funded question, yeah id run two profiles. the challenge only pays you for hitting +10 without breaking a rule, so profit above that is worth nothing and the extra dd is all downside. id size it so the worst monte carlo path sits well under the 9.5 cap and just accept that it takes longer

for forward testing id count trades. if the system does 5 a week, a month of demo is 20 trades and that tells you almost nothing. something like 50 to 100 before paying for the challenge, and compare the slippage you actually get on gold to what the backtest assumed

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
no, I'd stop chasing a bigger total. the challenge only pays for reaching the target, anything past it buys nothing and costs you room on the drawdown. tune for the fewest days to the target with the daily limit never closer than about 1%.

the 100% pass rate is the red flag you already smelled. reshuffling trades from one backtest only reorders the same trades, so it can't show you a market the backtest never saw. I'd rerun it on a year you didn't build it on, add a fixed cost to every fill (gold spreads blow out on news), and resample by whole weeks instead of single trades, because losing trades come in clusters.

if a model is making the calls, a 2025 backtest is weaker still, it may have read about those days. a month forward on demo with the rules frozen before you start, then buy the challenge.

comments.author: mehatebananas
comments.body:
Probably a broken backtest to begin with. Fees, slippage, lookahead bias, assumed fills, timestamp misalignments. There's a lot that can go into making a strategy look great on paper. I'd start by asking another agent to train itself on all the things that break a backtest and then ask it to audit everything. 

Or forward test it on a demo account for a few week and see how far off the results are from a backtest on that same data.
